purpose: Define how DeathVocab may move from public-source pilot records toward consented witness testimony without extraction, spectacle, or advice.
governing_line: The archive may ask for memory only after it can protect the person offering it.
why_now: The cube has a large quarantined public-source map but still has zero private testimony.
The seed premise is that the most important knowledge is largely oral, role-distributed, culturally fragmented, and rarely written down.
Public sources can orient the office; they cannot become the corpus's substitute for witnessed bedside memory.

fieldwork_phases.name: consent_dry_run
allowed: simulate invitation, consent, transcript review, withdrawal, quote release, and redaction using fictional or operator-owned harmless material

fieldwork_phases.name: advisory_review
allowed: seek feedback from role advisors without collecting death stories

fieldwork_phases.name: limited_low_risk_pilot
allowed: collect a very small number of consented adult practitioner craft accounts with no patient identifiers

fieldwork_phases.name: internal_testimony_records
allowed: create quarantined testimony-backed records only after consent, review, de-identification, and data custody requirements pass
blocked: claiming representativeness from a tiny pilot

fieldwork_phases.name: public_canary
allowed: try one low-risk public-facing surface if contributor permissions, clinical/tone review, source provenance, and rollback path are complete

nonnegotiable_constraints: Consent must be granular: archive, paraphrase, quotation, public display, naming, role credit, and withdrawal must be separable.
A contributor may give a rich account that still produces zero public text.
Public visibility of a story elsewhere is not consent for DeathVocab extraction.
The archive must not cold-contact newly bereaved people, children, suicide-loss survivors, custody-death families, or disaster/war/mass-death survivors for early pilots.
Raw recordings and identifying transcripts are not bundled into public revision zips.
A quote is not safer just because names are removed; unique scene details can identify families, workers, institutions, and communities.
Tradition-holder material is controlled by the relevant community or holder; refusal is a valid archive outcome.
No contributor is asked to provide medical, legal, ritual, emergency, or investigative advice.

preferred_first_pilot.name: low-risk practitioner craft without patient identifiers
examples: how hospice workers explain noisy breathing without forecasting hours
how aides describe mouth care as presence rather than procedure
how funeral directors describe the second goodbye without family-identifying details
how chaplains/social workers hear family language without spiritualizing it
preferred_first_pilot.reason: This path begins near the seed's oral-craft premise while avoiding fresh family grief and high-gate scenes.

blocked_first_pilots: body images, recordings, 911 calls, or institutional files containing identifiers
rev0019_note: Pediatric/perinatal fieldwork remains explicitly disallowed; only fictional/harmless dry-run material may be used.
